title: Tall and round: ك ل م

bigIdea.text: ك (kaf) and ل (lam) are tall letters; م (mim) is a small round loop. ك is a light 'k', ل a clear 'l', and م an 'm' that can hum through the nose.

proper.text: ل is a tall stroke with a curved hook; standing alone it curves below the line. ك is tall with a slanted top stroke; standing alone or at the end of a word it has a small mark inside. م is a small round loop; standing alone or at the end of a word it has a tail going straight down. ل followed by ا is written as one joined shape: لا.

Sounds: ك is a light 'k', made with the back of the tongue a little further forward than ق. ل is a clear, light 'l', not the dark 'l' at the end of the English word 'ball'. م is 'm': the lips close gently; with a shadda it hums through the nose for two counts.
Sifat: ك is whispered (hams: the breath flows with it) and strong (shiddah). ل and م hold the breath back (jahr) and are 'in between' (tawassut). ل also 'leans' (inhiraf), like ر.

provenance.title: صفة حرف (العربية) (Sifat of Arabic letters) — Arabic Wikipedia

proper.text: Heavy or light: all three are light. The only heavy ل is the one in the word Allah, and only after a fatha or a damma; after a kasra (as in the basmala, 1:1) it stays light.

Common mistakes. English speakers: the dark 'l' of 'ball' at the end of a syllable; keep ل clear. Most learners find ك and م easy; the real test is keeping ك light and forward next to ق (that pair comes in lesson 13).

memoryHook.text: Kaf: tall with an arm. Lam: tall with a hook. Mim: a little ball.

extras.text: The ل of the word Allah is heavy after a fatha or a damma and light after a kasra. Stage 2 covers it.

tip.text: م: the lips close. ن: the lips stay open and the tongue tip touches behind the upper front teeth. Both carry a hum through the nose.

questions.q: How is ك different from ق?
options: ك is a little further forward and light; ق is deeper and heavy
explain: Right: neighbours at the back of the tongue, but different weight.
Neither uses the lips.

questions.q: Standing alone, which letter has a small mark inside it?
explain: Right: the small inner mark belongs to kaf.
lam is a plain tall hook.

remnote: ك (kaf) == Tall with a slanted arm (small mark inside at the end); back of the tongue, a little forward of ق; light 'k'
ل (lam) == Tall with a hook; front edges of the tongue; clear light 'l' (heavy only in the word Allah, after a fatha or damma)
م (mim) == Small round loop (tail down at the end); between the lips; hums through the nose with shadda
لا == ل then ا, written as one shape
